summary: Round 4, scoped to the delta since 746ac9a9. F19 is correct: with new Checkpoint(...) and encode() inside the try, an unchecked throw from either now hits the finally, resets deltasSinceCheckpoint, leaves dirty set and leaves written false -- the counter reset and the dirty flag end up in opposite states on every exit, which is what the two comments claim. (The reachable-exception story is better than the comment admits: CommitRequest already refuses a null/blank podId and a negative flushSeq, and CommitLog offsets are non-negative, so Checkpoint's own IllegalArgumentException guards are unreachable from this writer and an Error really is all that is left.) F18 is correct on the question asked: close() writes the volatile closed before tickerThread.interrupt(), and JLS 17.4.4 gives the interrupt a synchronizes-with edge at the point the interrupt is detected, so a legitimate shutdown cannot log ERROR spuriously, and an abnormal interrupt is misread as a clean stop only if it races close() -- benign. F17's correction is at the site. The rounds:M4.8b2 line is keyed first, carries a reason, and is staged as an added line; its account checks out against .harness/review -- round 1 was 2 blocking + 5 major, all code (F1 data race, F2 counter-at-K, F5 fenced writer, F6 IAE stranding the lease), round 2's reviewer minors F12/F14 are fixes reintroducing what they fixed, and the four invented reasons are F9/F13/F16 plus the test javadoc. 'The code was wrong, repeatedly' is accurate. The three new tests encode requirements production already meets (checkPolicy and requireNonNull both precede tryAcquire; dirty survives an unchecked throw because only written clears it; the writer's key is checkpointKeyFor(nextSequence) at the log's own epoch), and none of them is satisfied vacuously -- RecordingBinStore records the PUT key before throwing and does not delegate, so the retry finds the key free. No request-rate change in the delta: the K trigger and the T trigger are untouched, and F19's move can only lower the failure-path PUT rate. Two minors, both about statements rather than behaviour, and both in text that has now been redrafted three times.

findings.title: The new ERROR line tells the operator checkpointing has stopped, when only the T trigger has -- and the comment 15 lines below it says the opposite
findings.failure_scenario: The message is 'the checkpoint ticker was interrupted without being closed; no further checkpoints will be written by this node', and the comment above it says returning 'ends checkpointing for the life of the process'. Neither is true. The K trigger does not live on the ticker thread: CheckpointWriter.capture ends with `if (deltasSinceCheckpoint >= everyDeltas) writeIfDirty();`, reached from observe on the commit thread, and nothing in tickForever's exit path sets closed or otherwise disables it. So after the ticker dies, a leader committing at or above K deltas per period keeps checkpointing at exactly the intended rate; it is only a leader below that rate that loses checkpointing entirely. The adjacent `catch (Throwable keepTicking)` comment already states the correct version -- 'below K deltas per period the T trigger is ALL there is' -- so the same method now carries two comments that disagree about what the ticker's death costs. Concretely: the store restores the interrupt and throws IOException from a checkpoint putIfAbsent (the BoundedLock.takeOrFail idiom the comment cites), the next Thread.sleep throws at once, this ERROR is logged on a busy leader, and an operator reading it as stated concludes the recovery bound is gone and fails the leader over. That failover burns an epoch and costs the successor a seal plus a full recover() -- one GET per delta of the term, as LocalSequencer.start's own comment records -- to fix a node that was still writing a checkpoint every K deltas. The same overstatement is in the backlog-done row's round-3 bullet ('checkpointing ends for the life of the process'). The accurate statement is the one already in the file: the T trigger is dead for the life of the process, and below K deltas per period that is all there was.
findings.suggestion: Say what died: '...the T trigger is dead for the life of this process; checkpoints now depend entirely on the K trigger.' Same for the comment above it and the backlog row's round-3 bullet. Cheap, but a fifth round is not -- record it in the commit body instead if that is the call.

findings.title: The putIfAbsent comment's enumeration is still one path short: it names only the IOException retry, and this same commit adds the test for the unchecked one
findings.failure_scenario: The comment now says 'the only way to find the key occupied is THIS writer retrying a PUT that reported IOException and had landed'. The unchecked path reaches the identical state and is modelled explicitly in this very diff: RecordingBinStore's javadoc calls it 'A DIFFERENT PATH FROM failNextCheckpointPut, not a variation on it', and the new anUNCHECKEDFailureLeavesTheWriterDirtySoALaterTickStillWrites pins that an unchecked throw leaves dirty set exactly as an IOException does -- because only `written` clears it. A real store can land the object and then throw unchecked (an SdkClientException raised after the write completes, a response-parse failure, an OOME in the client's response path); the retry then finds the key occupied with no 'was not written; retrying at the next trigger' WARNING ever emitted, because that message is only on the IOException branch. Failure scenario: someone debugging an occupied checkpoint key follows this comment, greps for the retry WARNING, finds none, and concludes the key must have been written by another writer -- i.e. diagnoses a fencing bug that the epoch-in-key makes impossible, which is the exact wrong conclusion this comment was rewritten twice to prevent. The 'USUALLY byte-identical' half is right this time (a throw between the pods.merge loop and the pendingSequence assignment does leave pods advanced with the sequence unmoved, and the landed body is the older one, which fold's Math::max makes safe).
findings.suggestion: Drop 'reported IOException' for 'failed after landing -- IOException or unchecked, and only the first of those logs a retry line'. Or delete the enumeration and keep the consequence, which is the remedy this task already applied to M4.8a's route count.
